tierWhy: The original Atari, Inc. was broken up and sold by Warner Communications in July 1984; the name now belongs to Atari SA, a Paris-listed publisher of retro games and hardware that reported €56.0M of revenue for the year to March 2026.[^7][^21]

place: Video games and home computers · Sunnyvale, California
title: Atari (1972–1984): collapse and the buried cartridges
description: Atari made the home video game a business, lost $538 million in 1983 and was sold by Warner for notes and no cash in 1984. Its name has been sold on ever since.

card.blurb: It grew to about $2 billion in sales in six years under Warner, lost $538 million the year after, and was handed to a rival for no cash. The name has been sold on ever since.

hero.dates: Founded 1972. Sold to Warner 1976. Broken up and sold Jul 2, 1984.
hero.standfirst: Atari made the home video game a business, and then showed how quickly that business could vanish.
hero.deck: Atari was the [video game](/category/games/) company that Warner Communications bought for $28 million in 1976 and gave to a competitor for notes and no cash in July 1984. By 1982 it was half of Warner’s revenue. One year later it had lost more than half a billion dollars, buried truckloads of cartridges in the New Mexico desert and laid off most of its staff. The name has since belonged to a disk-drive maker, a toy company and a French publisher, and it is still trading.

findings.title: It was half of Warner.
findings.text: In the first nine months of 1982 Atari contributed half of Warner’s $2.9 billion in revenue and two thirds of its $471 million in operating profit.[^1]

findings.title: The profit was in cartridges, and Atari lost its hold on them.
findings.text: An analyst put cartridges at $180 million of Atari’s $280 million operating profit in 1981. By December 1982 the number of game producers had more than tripled, to 20.[^1][^8]

findings.title: Management did not see it coming.
findings.text: Analysts said Warner privately confirmed their estimates until the morning before the December 8, 1982 warning. A Warner executive said the company was “blind-sided.”[^1]

findings.title: The collapse took one year.
findings.text: Atari earned $323 million in 1982 and lost $536 million in the first nine months of 1983. Staff fell from 10,000 to about 1,100 by June 1984.[^1][^6][^7]

findings.title: The name outlived the company by four decades.
findings.text: It was sold for $240 million in notes in 1984, for $5 million in 1998 and inside a $100 million deal in 2001. Its current owner reported €56.0M of revenue in FY2026.[^7][^13][^14][^21]
